newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Yu Sung files for court protection.
newsitem.headline: Yu Sung files for court protection.

text.p: South Korea's Yu Sung Co Ltd, a textile manufacturer, said on Wednesday it had filed for court protection late on Tuesday after defaulting on payments of 227 million won worth of promissory notes.
A company statement said its financial trouble stemmed from difficulties in obtaining operating funds and the depressed textile industry.
The Korea Stock Exchange said Yu Sung would be placed on a supervision list and trading of its stock would resume from Friday.
Trading of the stock was halted from Wednesday morning.
Yu Sung posted a net profit of 437 million won last year on turnover of 57.58 billion. At the end of 1996, its paid-in capital stood at 15 billion won and liabilities at 66.6 billion.
Yu Sung's trouble follows a string of corporate insolvencies in South Korea this year, starting with the collapse of Hanbo Steel in January and Sammi Steel in March.
The Jinro Group managed to avoid a collapse last month only after banks agreed to a rescue.
The Ssangyong and Doosan groups have announced major restructuring plans in recent weeks. Both have said they will sell real estate and merge or sell affiliates.
